mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where RSAFS shows a 3-month decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past 3 months, coupled with a decrease in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.1% in the same period, signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decrease > 5% and PAYEMS decrease > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST and PAYEMS both show the specified declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% annually and Housing Starts (HOUST) are decreasing, it indicates a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth < 2% and HOUST decreasing
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where GDPC1 growth is below 2% annually and HOUST is decreasing.
